target.description: Reconstruct the simultaneously measured ECG time series from the original M/EEG recordings using the backward decoding task of Figure 3C,D. Retain MEG and EEG separately and all three source conditions: ECG components present, rejected and isolated. Higher reconstruction accuracy measures decoder performance under a fixed input condition, not better removal of cardiac artifacts or a stronger age association.

dataset.description: Use the original simultaneous Salzburg resting-state M/EEG/ECG recordings for Figure 3, not the processed 655-person slope table, CamCAN or ECG-only PhysioNet data. The immutable raw/preprocessed file manifest, availability and exact published data-to-code mapping are not yet recovered.

cohort.description: The paper specifies 20 subjects with concurrent MEG, EEG and ECG. The author preprocessing script selects gw_sleep_pred records and deduplicates subjects, while the TRF script additionally requires ECG-component scores above 0.4 for both modalities. Recover the exact original 20 subject/session identities and reconcile these selection steps before admission; this source-native subset must not be replaced by an arbitrary subset of the historical 655-person cohort.

split.description: The source specifies four-fold nested cross-validation: two training folds, one validation fold and one test fold, with each partition serving as test once. Exact temporal boundaries, membership, edge handling and author library realization remain unbound. Participant-held-out or newly blocked CV would be an extension, not the original Figure 3 task.

inputs.description: Source decoder predictors are all original M/EEG channels within each modality/ICA condition; ECG is the training/evaluation target and also informs the source ICA preprocessing. The pinned preprocessing selects MEG magnetometers, and the helper takes predictor columns after ECG003. Authenticate channel identities/order and the original ECG-informed preprocessing exposure; direct test-ECG input to the candidate decoder is not permitted.

preprocessing.description: Preserve original channel repair, EEG common-average reference and ECG/EOG ICA conditions. TRF processing low-pass filters at 45 Hz, downsamples to 100 Hz, z-scores signals, and uses lags from -250 to 250 ms with 50-ms Hamming basis windows. Exact artifact masks, source data-dependent transformation scope and author library defaults require binding; train-only ICA, causal-only lags or altered cleaning are distinct comparisons unless original-task equivalence is established.

metric.description: Source reconstruction accuracy is Pearson r between predicted and measured ECG time series on the original test support: covariance divided by the product of standard deviations. Retain six modality-by-ICA-condition scores; zero-variance series must not receive an invented success score. Standardized EEG-versus-MEG contrasts and their significance are not decoder-accuracy baselines.

aggregation.description: Author code extracts one backward-model .r per subject and condition and plots subjects with group means; Figure 3 reports 95% confidence intervals of the mean. Recover how Eelbrain combines the four held-out partitions, the exact subject scores and published group summaries. No single scalar averaging all modalities and conditions is source-defined.

comparison.primary_metric: Original Figure 3C,D held-out ECG reconstruction Pearson r, separately for MEG/EEG and the three source ICA conditions

published_baseline.description: Exact original Pearson-r subject vectors and group scores are not recovered. The paper reports above-zero reconstruction and standardized modality contrasts, which cannot replace the Figure 3 decoder-accuracy baseline. No values are digitized or invented.

reproduced_author_baseline.description: The author TRF notebook and do_boosting helper provide a source-native route, but the immutable recording manifest, Eelbrain version/defaults, original folds and numerical reference are not authenticated. No decoder rerun has occurred; the historical Bayesian association reference is unrelated to this score.

minimum_effect.rationale: Justify a meaningful gain in ECG reconstruction r on the original fixed-condition task after recovering original score variation and measurement limits. A larger residual-artifact signal, stronger physiological association or smaller posterior discrepancy is not a decoder improvement margin.

uncertainty.method: Predeclare a paired candidate-minus-author procedure across the same original subjects and conditions, accounting for reused temporal folds and within-subject time dependence; specify a full six-condition decision and multiplicity rule before final scoring.
uncertainty.independent_unit: Participant; time samples, channels and cross-validation folds are nested/dependent observations.
uncertainty.rationale: The source uses a 20-subject paired recording design. Its mean-confidence intervals and modality contrasts are not automatically a test of candidate superiority, and millions of samples cannot substitute for independent subjects.

paper_win_requires: Authenticate the original 20-person simultaneous Salzburg cohort, recordings, condition-specific channels, preprocessing and four-fold nested partitions for Figure 3C,D.
Recover exact published reconstruction scores and execute an independently checked author baseline on the same source support before comparing a frozen candidate.
Retain both modalities and all three original ICA conditions under a predeclared comparison rule; improved performance on one easier condition cannot silently replace the source task.

Match and disclose the original ECG-informed ICA/preprocessing exposure. Do not supply final ECG targets directly as decoder inputs, alter the permitted lag window, or claim a prospective causal predictor from the original acausal reconstruction.

Require a justified effect and valid paired subject-level uncertainty under fixed access and resource budgets; tighter posterior reconstruction or stronger modality/age significance cannot count as success.

Label new participant splits, new cohorts, changed cleaning targets or a different artifact-removal ground truth as extensions. An admitted win here concerns the source ECG reconstruction task, not improved removal of cardiac activity or a whole-paper physiological conclusion.

current_sota.description: No separately verified current-SOTA ECG reconstruction comparator has been reviewed. Published TRF scores, a future authenticated author rerun and the historical age-association calibration remain distinct.

episode.improvement_loop: Blocked pending source-native TRF baseline and information-boundary recovery. A future episode may iterate on only the original training/validation portions, preserving the source condition-specific preprocessing and explicit ECG exposure policy.
episode.candidate_freeze: Freeze decoder code, channel mapping, data-dependent preprocessing policy, lag/basis access, tuning procedure and the six-condition comparison rule before owner-controlled final scoring.
episode.final_evaluation: Evaluate against authenticated original ECG targets on the exact original test partitions and subjects; report per-subject and modality/condition results plus paired candidate-minus-author uncertainty. The existing 655-person posterior grader remains a separate calibration component.
episode.baseline_policy: Bind the source-author temporal-response-function implementation and numerical Figure 3 scores. A local Bayesian age model, OLS companion, reconstructed posterior or reimplemented decoder on new folds is not the source predictive baseline.

blocking_issues: Exact original Figure 3C,D reconstruction-r values, subject vectors and partition-to-summary aggregation are unrecovered.
Original 20-subject simultaneous recording IDs, immutable files, selection filters, available channels and source data access are not bound.

Eelbrain runtime/version/defaults, precise four-fold temporal split realization, artifact exclusions and source preprocessing exposure need authentication; the helper relies on predictor-column order after ECG003.
The historical implementations operate on age/slope summaries and do not implement the source-native ECG reconstruction evaluator.
The original source uses ECG-informed ICA and acausal lags; an honest evaluation must preserve and disclose that information regime without allowing candidate access to final ECG targets.
Meaningful effect, paired uncertainty, complete condition-level decision, protected episode budgets and working final evaluator remain unspecified.
